comment: Cross-impl vectors for TEE measurement arithmetic. Regenerate via: cd proto/go && go test ./attest -run TestVectors -update. Loaded by proto/go/attest/vectors_test.go and proto/ts/test/attest-vectors.test.ts. Inputs are the capture files named below, not inlined here.

report_data.name: non-ASCII pubkey is hashed as UTF-8

h_app.name: empty catalog is the pending value
h_app.why: Must equal HAppPending. Neither may be 32 zero bytes, or a booting node is indistinguishable from a pre-9.9 one and the check is skipped exactly when it is least earned.

h_app.name: one measured model
h_app.why: The ordinary case.

h_app.name: one declared model
h_app.why: THE PAIR for 'one measured model': byte-identical to it except the state, so the digests differ ONLY because the state byte does. A mirror collapsing the two states produces one digest for two different claims, and this is the case that catches it — which it cannot do if any other field also moves.

h_app.name: one unverifiable model carries no digest
h_app.why: Hosted passthrough. The empty digest is the point: absence is a VALUE here, so this must not collide with a model omitted from the catalog entirely.

h_app.name: three models, given sorted
h_app.why: Paired with the next case: both must produce the SAME digest, which is what pins that sorting happens inside HApp rather than being the caller's duty.

h_app.name: three models, given unsorted
h_app.why: THE PAIR. A node builds its catalog from maps and discovery order; if input order changed the digest, a node and a verifier holding identical sets would disagree with nothing to diagnose it.

h_app.name: model ids sort by BYTES, not by case
h_app.why: 'Z' (0x5a) sorts BELOW 'a' (0x61). A mirror using localeCompare or a case-insensitive sort orders these the other way and digests a different preimage.

h_app.name: non-ASCII model id is length-prefixed in BYTES
h_app.why: lenStr counts UTF-8 bytes; JavaScript's String.length counts UTF-16 units, and they differ here. A mirror using .length writes a short length and every following field slides.

h_app.name: sort order is UTF-8 BYTES, not UTF-16 code units
h_app.why: THE ONLY CASE THAT CAN CATCH A PLAIN `a < b` IN THE MIRROR. Go compares strings bytewise, JavaScript's < compares UTF-16 code units, and these two ids order OPPOSITELY under the two rules: U+FFFD is EF BF BD in UTF-8 and 0xFFFD in UTF-16, while U+1F600 is F0 9F 98 80 in UTF-8 and the surrogate pair 0xD83D 0xDE00 in UTF-16 — so UTF-8 puts U+FFFD first and UTF-16 puts the emoji first. Every other multi-entry case here is ASCII, where the two rules agree, so deleting the TS compareUtf8 helper passes the whole suite without this one. Unreachable over the wire today; it is here because the divergence it pins is silent and the vector is free.

h_app.name: empty source is allowed
h_app.why: A model whose provenance the node resolved to nothing is legitimate, and its empty lenStr must still occupy four bytes.

h_app.name: duplicate model ids are REFUSED even when nothing else matches
h_app.why: They cannot both answer 'what is this node serving as m', and a minter and a verifier breaking the tie differently compute different digests from identical input. The two entries agree on the ID AND NOTHING ELSE on purpose: a check that also compared source or state would still refuse two exact clones, so only a pair like this one — the shape an operator would actually build to slip a substituted model past an id-matching verifier — pins that the ID ALONE is the key.

h_app.name: duplicate detected across an unsorted input
h_app.why: The dedup runs after the sort, so an adjacent-pair check must still catch a pair the caller separated. These two ARE exact clones, which is what keeps that easier case covered once the vector above stopped being one.

h_app.name: model ids that are PREFIXES of one another
h_app.why: Sorting falls through to the length tiebreak only when one id is a prefix of the other, and every other multi-entry case here differs at some byte or has equal lengths — so this is the only case that pins the tail of the comparison. Unlike the surrogate-pair case above, this shape is not exotic: 'llama-3' and 'llama-3-instruct' is what a real catalog looks like, so a mirror reversing the tiebreak diverges on ordinary input.

h_app.name: empty model id is REFUSED
h_app.why: Nothing can match it against a request, so it can only pad the count.

h_app.name: measured with no digest is REFUSED
h_app.why: The state claims the node hashed something and the entry shows nothing.

h_app.name: DECLARED with no digest is REFUSED
h_app.why: THE THIRD CORNER of the state/digest matrix, and the one a mirror is likeliest to drop: measured and declared share a branch here, so splitting them and letting declared through refuses nothing the other two cases test. Declared is a weaker claim than measured but it is still a claim, and an entry asserting it while showing no digest would otherwise fold into an attested catalog with nothing behind it.

h_app.name: unverifiable WITH a digest is REFUSED
h_app.why: The other direction, and the one a lenient mirror is likelier to allow: it looks like extra information rather than a contradiction.

h_app.name: an unknown state byte is REFUSED
h_app.why: Fail closed. A newer node's state would otherwise be hashed as one this verifier thinks it understands.

h_app.name: state zero is REFUSED
h_app.why: 0 is the Go zero value and what a lenient JSON decoder yields for a missing weights_state. It must not mean measured, the strongest claim.

h_app.name: an entry breaking TWO rules reports the FIRST one
h_app.why: Pins the check order, so Go and TypeScript report the same code for one input. The empty id is checked before the state.

aux_binding.name: node id zero, pending catalog
aux_binding.why: A little-endian implementation agrees with a big-endian one on id 0 and on nothing else, so this case alone cannot tell them apart — it is here to pair with the ones below.

aux_binding.name: node id above 32 bits
aux_binding.why: Catches a 32-bit truncation that every small id hides.

aux_binding.name: max uint64 node id
aux_binding.why: The boundary that forces node_id to ride as a decimal string rather than a JSON number.

aux_binding.name: explicit all-zero nonce
aux_binding.why: THE PAIR: it must produce the IDENTICAL digest to an absent nonce, because absent IS 32 zero bytes. That is why 'I supplied a nonce and got zeros back' cannot be detected here and must be a verifier-side failure — this function cannot see what was asked for.

aux_binding.name: a real nonce
aux_binding.why: The on-demand ?nonce= path. Different digest for the same catalog and node, which is the whole point of liveness.

aux_binding.name: a named-upstream posture
aux_binding.why: H_posture sits between H_app and the nonce; swapping the two 32-byte fields must change the digest, which only a case with both non-trivial can show.

h_app_json.name: well-formed entry
h_app_json.why: The control for the cases below.

h_app_json.name: measured entry with weights_digest missing
h_app_json.why: A lenient decoder reads the missing digest as "" and refuses measured-without-digest; JavaScript reads undefined, which is not "", and used to hash it as a measured claim with no digest. Both must refuse it as malformed.

h_app_json.name: measured entry with a null weights_digest
h_app_json.why: JavaScript's TextEncoder encodes null as the four bytes "null".

h_app_json.name: null source
h_app_json.why: Go decodes null into a string as ""; JavaScript keeps null.

h_app_json.name: model_id missing
h_app_json.why: Go decodes it as "" and reports an empty id; JavaScript used to hash undefined as an empty string without the empty-id check firing.

h_app_json.name: weights_state missing
h_app_json.why: A lenient Go decoder reads 0.

h_app_json.name: weights_state zero
h_app_json.why: A present 0 is well-formed JSON and an unknown state.

h_app_json.name: weights_state above 255
h_app_json.why: Go cannot store 300 in a uint8. It must be an unknown state in both implementations, not a decode failure in one.

h_app_json.name: weights_state 257
h_app_json.why: 257 truncates to 1 in a uint8, so a decoder missing the upper bound reads it as measured. 300 truncates to 44, still unknown, and cannot tell.

h_app_json.name: weights_state -255
h_app_json.why: -255 wraps to 1 in a uint8, so a decoder missing the lower bound reads it as measured.

h_app_json.name: weights_state null
h_app_json.why: Malformed, not unknown: null into a Go float64 is a silent 0.

h_app_json.name: weights_state 1.0
h_app_json.why: JSON.parse yields 1, so Go accepts it too. Same digest as the well-formed entry.

h_app_json.name: weights_state 1.5
h_app_json.why: Not an integer.

h_app_json.name: weights_state as a string
h_app_json.why: Wrong type.

h_app_json.name: model_id as a number
h_app_json.why: Wrong type.

h_app_json.name: key in the wrong case
h_app_json.why: Go's default struct decoding matches keys case-insensitively; JavaScript does not. The strict decoder matches exactly.

h_app_json.name: an extra key is ignored
h_app_json.why: Both implementations ignore unknown keys. Same digest as the well-formed entry.

h_app_json.name: a null entry
h_app_json.why: Not an object.

h_app_json.name: a number entry
h_app_json.why: Not an object.

h_app_json.name: lone surrogates decode to one id
h_app_json.why: Go's decoder turns an unpaired surrogate escape into U+FFFD, so these are duplicates in Go. JavaScript keeps the lone surrogates as distinct strings; its verifier must compare UTF-8 bytes, where TextEncoder also writes U+FFFD.

h_app_json.name: malformed is checked before the per-entry rules
h_app_json.why: The empty-id entry sorts first, but the malformed-entry pass runs over the whole list before sorting, so the code is malformed_model_entry.

h_app_json.name: duplicate ids keep their input order
h_app_json.why: The sort is stable, so the valid "dup" stays first and the second is reported as a duplicate. An unstable sort (Go's pdqsort above 12 elements) can put the bad-state copy first and report unknown_weights_state instead.

aux_verify.name: unchallenged cached bundle
aux_verify.why: The ordinary case.

aux_verify.name: challenged, echo matches
aux_verify.why: The ?nonce= path.

aux_verify.name: challenged, echo in upper case
aux_verify.why: Both implementations decode hex case-insensitively and compare bytes.

aux_verify.name: challenged, echo absent
aux_verify.why: A replayed cached bundle. Hashing 32 zero bytes would verify it; the verifier must refuse because it asked for a nonce.

aux_verify.name: challenged, echo is another caller's nonce
aux_verify.why: A replayed bundle minted for someone else's challenge. Its binding is valid for the nonce it carries, so hashing the echo would verify it.

aux_verify.name: challenged, echo malformed
aux_verify.why: Refused as a nonce mismatch, not a malformed nonce: the verifier asked for a specific value.

aux_verify.name: unchallenged, bundle carries a nonce
aux_verify.why: A bundle minted for another caller's challenge still verifies for a verifier that sent none.

aux_verify.name: unchallenged, nonce not hex
aux_verify.why: Refused rather than read as absent.

aux_verify.name: unchallenged, nonce too short
aux_verify.why: Exactly 64 hex characters or refused.

aux_verify.name: sibling node's bundle
aux_verify.why: Minted by node 8, checked against node 7's chain-resolved id.

aux_verify.name: empty catalog, honest
aux_verify.why: A node serving nothing, or still booting. Verifies.

aux_verify.name: catalog withheld
aux_verify.why: The quote commits to a catalog the bundle does not publish.

aux_verify.name: sibling node's empty-catalog bundle
aux_verify.why: Also happ_preimage_missing: with no entries, a node-id mismatch and a withheld catalog cannot be told apart.

aux_verify.name: catalog edited in transit
aux_verify.why: A relay changed a digest.

aux_verify.name: malformed catalog
aux_verify.why: Refused before the comparison.

aux_verify.name: nonce is checked before the catalog
aux_verify.why: Pins the order: a nonce mismatch is reported even when the catalog is also malformed.

aux_verify.name: challenge is all zero
aux_verify.why: Zeros hash the same as no nonce, so a cached bundle with a 64-zero nonce field would pass as fresh. The verifier's own challenge is refused.

aux_verify.name: challenge starts with a zero byte
aux_verify.why: Only an all-zero challenge is refused. A check on the first byte would refuse one honest random challenge in 256.

aux_verify.name: app_models is null
aux_verify.why: Go decodes null as an absent list; TypeScript must treat it the same, not as a malformed list.

aux_verify.name: app_models is null, catalog withheld
aux_verify.why: null must reach the missing-catalog check, not fail on reading the list.

aux_verify.name: app_models is [], catalog withheld
aux_verify.why: An explicit empty list is the same claim as an absent one.

aux_verify.name: unchallenged, nonce too long
aux_verify.why: The echo is node-controlled; 66 hex characters must be refused, not decoded into 32 bytes past the end.

aux_verify.name: catalog with a duplicate id
aux_verify.why: Each HApp refusal is happ_preimage_invalid, not a disagreement.

aux_verify.name: catalog with an empty id
aux_verify.why: As above.

aux_verify.name: catalog whose state contradicts its digest
aux_verify.why: As above.

aux_verify.name: catalog with an unknown state
aux_verify.why: As above.

aux_verify.name: posture honest
aux_verify.why: The attested_passthrough case: the published posture is the one the quote commits to.

aux_verify.name: posture URL rewritten in transit
aux_verify.why: The lookalike attack against an honest node: the binary signed api.x.ai, a relay publishes an attacker host. Refused.

aux_verify.name: posture signed with the lookalike
aux_verify.why: The binding verifies — it proves only what the binary derived. Judging the URL is the verifier's next step, not this one.

aux_verify.name: zero_retention flipped on
aux_verify.why: A relay upgrading the flag.

aux_verify.name: posture stripped
aux_verify.why: The quote commits to a posture the bundle no longer carries.

aux_verify.name: posture added
aux_verify.why: The quote commits to no posture; the bundle carries one.

aux_verify.name: posture null
aux_verify.why: null is absent: the same digest, so it verifies against an absent-posture quote.

aux_verify.name: posture stripped, empty catalog
aux_verify.why: With no entries every mismatch reads happ_preimage_missing — the digest cannot say which input moved.

aux_verify.name: upstream_attested set in transit
aux_verify.why: A relay claiming the node appraises its upstream, to pair with an injected upstream_attestation block. Refused.

h_posture.name: absent
h_posture.why: No posture field. Committed as absent, so a relay cannot add one.

h_posture.name: null
h_posture.why: Go decodes null into a nil pointer: the same claim as absent, and the same digest.

h_posture.name: in_enclave
h_posture.why: The sealed_local posture: no upstream, no zero-retention flag.

h_posture.name: named upstream, xAI
h_posture.why: The attested_passthrough case this binding exists for.

h_posture.name: named upstream, zero_retention false
h_posture.why: Paired with the previous case: the flag alone must move the digest.

h_posture.name: named upstream, lookalike host
h_posture.why: One changed host: a different digest, so a relay cannot swap the URL a verifier judges.

h_posture.name: explicit nulls inside
h_posture.why: Go leaves a string or bool field at its zero value on null; TypeScript must read null as '' and false, or the two hash different postures.

h_posture.name: empty object
h_posture.why: Present but empty is NOT absent: the presence byte differs.

h_posture.name: unknown key
h_posture.why: An unrecognised key is ignored by both decoders and does not enter the preimage.

h_posture.name: non-ASCII URL
h_posture.why: Lengths are UTF-8 byte counts, not UTF-16 code units.

h_posture.name: field boundary
h_posture.why: lenStr framing: moving bytes between two adjacent strings must change the digest.

h_posture.name: named upstream, attested gateway
h_posture.why: The ACI gateway posture: the bound upstream_attested bit, which a relay cannot set.

h_posture.name: bool order
h_posture.why: zero_retention and upstream_attested swapped: the two flag bytes are positional.

hostile.name: uppercase hex payload
hostile.why: Go's hex.DecodeString takes either case; a mirror that lowercased its charset would reject a log Go accepts.

hostile.name: lowercase 0x prefix
hostile.why: Trimmed by both, so this is the case that keeps the next one from being read as 'prefixes are rejected'.

hostile.name: uppercase 0X prefix
hostile.why: THE DIVERGENCE. Go trims only lowercase, so 0X reaches hex.DecodeString and fails; a mirror accepting 0X decodes and routes on evidence Go refuses.

hostile.name: null event name
hostile.why: JSON null lands as the empty string in Go. A mirror using a non-nullish coalesce hashes the four bytes 'null' and gets a different RTMR3 from the same log.

hostile.name: absent event_payload
hostile.why: Absent decodes to the empty payload and still extends. A mirror that treated undefined as undecodable would refuse a log Go accepts.

hostile.name: empty event name is measured by nobody
hostile.why: RuntimeMeasurements skips it; a mirror dropping that guard mints an empty-string key.

hostile.name: a later duplicate cannot displace a measured value
hostile.why: First occurrence wins, so an appended event cannot overwrite one the hardware measured.

hostile.name: a non-empty digest field is still ignored
hostile.why: dstack leaves digest empty; a mirror that trusted a populated one would extend with attacker-chosen bytes.

hostile.name: imr 3 but not a runtime event
hostile.why: Filtering on imr rather than event_type selects this; the two predicates disagree here and agree on the real capture.

hostile.name: runtime event outside imr 3
hostile.why: The converse: an imr filter would MISS this one.

hostile.name: odd-length payload
hostile.why: Not decodable as bytes; skipping it silently would yield a partial replay indistinguishable from a whole one.
